title: The Armor That Walks
text: A suit of black plate stands in the barrow's mouth, dented by blows that killed whoever wore it last. As you come close it turns its empty helm, slowly, toward the one of you who has killed the least. Then it opens its arms, the way a mother does.

options.label: Let the gentlest of you put it on.

outcomes.text: The plates close over them one by one. When the helm shuts, the eyes inside are not quite theirs any more.
It is only armor after all: very old, very good, and it fits.
It was not empty. It never was.

options.label: The strongest breaks it apart before it moves again.

outcomes.text: It comes apart like a dropped pot, and something sighs out of the pieces.
It does not want to be broken.
It watches you go. That night it is standing at the edge of the firelight, helm turned toward the camp, and nobody sleeps well.
It watches you go, and then it is not where you left it. You hear plate on stone behind you for the rest of the day.
